opportunities.title: supertet-policy-bound-binance-agent
opportunities.summary: ## Problem Statement Binance Agent OS lets an AI agent trade on your account. Its own launch coverage named the problem it left open: agents can trade, "but keeping them in check is largely up to users." The controls that exist are real but coarse. You grant OAuth scopes once, at connect time, and from then on the agent may trade anything those scopes cover, at any size, for as long as the authorization lasts. Confirm-before-execute catches each individual order, but it puts the person in the position of judging every order in isolation, with no standing statement of what they actually authorized and no running total of what has been spent against it. The only recorded limits are the scopes themselves, which cannot express "up to 200 USDT a day, spot only, BTC and ETH, until Friday." So the person funding the sub-account cannot answer the question that decides whether they leave the agent running: what is the worst case, in numbers, before it happens? ## Solution supertet is a policy-bound trading agent for Binance. opportunities.title: Python CLI interprets memory text as Rich markup, losing tags or failing reads
opportunities.summary: At main `7163538913e15dd86534b41dc695e2a5639c0774`, the Python CLI interprets API data as Rich markup. For a memory containing `Remember [bold]literal[/bold]`, both `omi --no-color memory get m1` and `omi --no-color memory list` silently remove the bracketed tags. A memory containing `Remember [/bold]` makes both commands fail with `MarkupError` (exit 1 through Typer's CliRunner). The corresponding `--json` commands preserve both strings and exit 0. This is a display/read failure; no stored-data loss is claimed. Minimal reproduction from `sdks/python-cli/` after installing its dependencies: ```python from omi_cli.output import Renderer Renderer(no_color=True).emit({'content': 'Remember [bold]literal[/bold]'}) # Displays: Remember literal (literal tags lost) Renderer(no_color=True).emit({'content': 'Remember [/bold]'}) # rich.errors.MarkupError ``` I also exercised the real `memory get` and `memory list` commands with synthetic HTTP 200 responses intercepted by respx: all four pretty-mode cases lose text or fail; all four JSON controls pass.
